queue_items.claim: The front-seam warrant's own contrast is not byte-supported: the 'second-person address' versus 'first-person-plural admission' opposition fails because the second half of the same verse opens on second-person address too, and first-person-plural verbs already stand in the preceding panel.
queue_items.grounds: oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5 opens its second half on הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier), second-person address identical in person to the first half's פָּגַ֤עְתָּ ... בִּדְרָכֶ֖יךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier); the only genuinely new element is the first-person-plural verb וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier). First-person-plural verbs already stand in the preceding panel at הָיִ֗ינוּ (oshb:Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.63.19, the split verse's first half, byte tier) and נְקַוֶּ֑ה (oshb:Isa.64.2 = web:Isa.64.3, byte tier). The row's underlying fact re-verifies -- no confession-of-sin verb stands anywhere in oshb:Isa.63.15-Isa.64.3 -- so the seam itself survives; only the stated contrast is defective.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair: re-cut the contrast to rest on the first-person-plural confession verb alone (spliced at oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5) and drop the person-shift framing, which the same verse's own bytes contradict.

queue_items.claim: The rear-seam hinge device -- 'a final unanswered double question', carried into observed_substrate_signals as speech_formula.unanswered_closing_question -- is established only from the WEB rendering's two question marks; the row carries no Hebrew splice or accent citation at its own closing verse, where a single interrogative particle governs both clauses across the caesura.
queue_items.grounds: oshb:Isa.64.11 = web:Isa.64.12 reads הַעַל אֵ֥לֶּה תִתְאַפַּ֖ק יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier) / תֶּחֱשֶׁ֥ה וּתְעַנֵּ֖נוּ עַד מְאֹֽד (byte tier): ONE interrogative he, on the first token, with the atnach on the fourth token; the second clause carries no interrogative particle of its own. The row's only citation for the 'double question' is the curly-quoted WEB run at web:Isa.64.12, which re-checks verbatim but is a tier-4 translation-punctuation fact. The answering divine reply that carries the same seam is likewise asserted at oshb:Isa.65.1 with no Hebrew splice anywhere in the row.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair: splice the interrogative particle and the atnach position at oshb:Isa.64.11 = web:Isa.64.12 and re-ground the closure device in the Hebrew, or re-label the observed_substrate_signals key so it does not rest on the translation's sentence punctuation.

queue_items.claim: frontier_flag_considered is false while the row's own device_notes calls the confession onset 'a soft, tonal seam rather than a formal header', and the book-order neighbour that owns the other side of the identical seam flags that same ground as a genuine frontier question.
queue_items.grounds: This row (span Isa.64.5-Isa.64.12) sets frontier_flag_considered false; the previous row (span Isa.63.15-Isa.64.4) sets it true and states the ground as the seam separating petition-recollection from confession being argued from a rhetorical-mode shift rather than a formal header. Both rows argue the same web:Isa.64.4 | web:Isa.64.5 (= oshb:Isa.64.3 | oshb:Isa.64.4) seam, from the same ground, at the same medium_low confidence. No formal signal stands at the seam: oshb:Isa.64.4 opens on the verb פָּגַ֤עְתָּ (byte tier) with no vocative, messenger frame, speaker change or addressee change from oshb:Isa.64.3, and the paragraph-mark inventory records no petuchah or setumah at MT 64:3 (single-witness; absence not counterevidence).
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair: set frontier_flag_considered true, matching both the neighbour row and this row's own stated ground.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The confession turns on a self-accusation standing mid-verse, after the verse's own caesura at יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4, byte tier), whose first half, פָּגַ֤עְתָּ אֶת שָׂשׂ֙ וְעֹ֣שֵׂה צֶ֔דֶק בִּדְרָכֶ֖יךָ יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4, byte tier), is second-person address continuing the preceding praise: "הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א" (oshb:Isa.64.4, byte tier) (web:Isa.64.5, 'Behold, you were angry, and we sinned'), a first-person-plural admission that has no counterpart in the preceding petition/recollection panel. The unit develops the confession -- “we have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteousness is like a polluted garment” (web:Isa.64.6) -- and moves to a closing series of direct imperative pleas, “Don't be furious, Yahweh. Don't remember iniquity forever.” (web:Isa.64.9), reporting the ruined holy cities and temple (web:Isa.64.10 = oshb:Isa.64.9 through web:Isa.64.11 = oshb:Isa.64.10) before closing on a final unanswered double question, “Will you hold yourself back for these things, Yahweh? Will you keep silent and punish us very severely?” (web:Isa.64.12). The unit ends there because oshb:Isa.65.1 answers this very question with a first-person divine reply, a scene and speaker change that the paragraph-mark inventory also brackets: a SAMEKH break sits at this unit's own close (oshb:Isa.64.11 = web:Isa.64.12).
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Isa.64.12-Isa.64.12 = oshb:Isa.64.11 (SAMEKH, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration, closes this unit)
web:Isa.64.4-Isa.64.4 (MT 64:3; cited for the rejected-alternative seam discussion)
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Setting the confession's onset at web:Isa.64.4 (= oshb:Isa.64.3) rather than web:Isa.64.5 (= oshb:Isa.64.4) was considered, since a mandated rival reading treats 64:4's 'from of old men have not heard' as already confessional in tone; it is rejected here because oshb:Isa.64.3 opens on a plain waw-conjunction, וּמֵעוֹלָ֥ם (oshb:Isa.64.3, byte tier), and runs to its own close still affirming Yahweh's incomparable work, יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה לִמְחַכֵּה לֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.64.3, byte tier), rather than opening a confession, and the unambiguous self-accusation 'we sinned' first appears at web:Isa.64.5 (= oshb:Isa.64.4).

shipped_row.device_notes: Filed under hymn_doxology as the closing panel of the larger communal-lament complex, again a confession/petition deviation disclosed rather than a sung-praise unit proper. Held at medium_low confidence because the exact confession onset (web:Isa.64.4-Isa.64.4 (MT 64:3) vs. web:Isa.64.5-Isa.64.5 (MT 64:4)) is a soft, tonal seam rather than a formal header -- the rival is disclosed above. The disclosure inventory records a SAMEKH break at this unit's own final verse (oshb:Isa.64.11 = web:Isa.64.12; single-witness, tier-3, not a driver), which corroborates but does not itself argue the boundary into web:Isa.65.1.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The petition opens with an imperative addressed directly to Yahweh, "הַבֵּ֤ט מִשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙" (oshb:Isa.63.15, byte tier) ('Look down from heaven'), rendered “Look down from heaven, and see” (web:Isa.63.15) -- a tier-1 vocative/imperative onset per the addressee-shift class, distinct from the third-person recollection that precedes it. The petition runs through the single MT verse that spans two WEB verses: the never-ruled complaint "הָיִ֗ינוּ מֵֽעוֹלָם֙ לֹֽא מָשַׁ֣לְתָּ בָּ֔ם לֹֽא נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם" (oshb:Isa.63.19, byte tier) lives at web:Isa.63.19 ('we have become like those from of old you never ruled, your name not called upon them'), and the same MT verse's tear-the-heavens plea "לוּא קָרַ֤עְתָּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ יָרַ֔דְתָּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ" (oshb:Isa.63.19, byte tier) lives at web:Isa.64.1 ('oh that you would tear the heavens, you would come down, the mountains would quake'); both halves belong to this row because they are one Hebrew sentence sharing one verse's bytes, and a row boundary is not argued between them. The theophany imagery continues past the split (fire kindling brushwood, the nations trembling, mountains quaking again at 64:2-3) and the unit closes at the affirmation "לֹֽא רָאָ֗תָה אֱלֹהִים֙ זוּלָ֣תְךָ֔" (oshb:Isa.64.3, byte tier) (web:Isa.64.4, 'the eye has not seen a God besides you'), immediately before the confessional turn “Behold, you were angry, and we sinned.” (web:Isa.64.5) opens a different speech-act.

web:Isa.64.1-Isa.64.1 = oshb:Isa.63.19 (second half of the split verse)
oshb:Isa.63.19-Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.63.19 (split verse; content argued here lives at BOTH web:Isa.63.19 and web:Isa.64.1)
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through the rest of the surrounding communal-lament complex as a single unbroken unit was considered and rejected here because the confessional turn at 64:5 ('Behold, you were angry, and we sinned') is a distinct rhetorical mode from the imperative petition and theophany recollection that occupy this row's own span, even though all three panels remain one liturgical whole in device_notes; a second, narrower alternative -- cutting a row boundary between web:Isa.63.19 and web:Isa.64.1 at the chapter line -- is rejected outright because the two WEB verses share one MT verse's bytes by construction and a boundary is not argued between them from their own content.

prev_row.device_notes: Filed under hymn_doxology as the operative category for this liturgical complex's middle panel; the content is petition and theophany-recollection rather than praise, disclosed here as a deviation. Held at medium_low confidence and flagged as a genuine frontier question because the exact seam separating petition-recollection from confession is argued from a rhetorical-mode shift rather than a formal header, and because this row carries the book's one split-verse pair (MT 63:19 = web:Isa.63.19 + web:Isa.64.1): every reference to either half above names which half it lives in, and the two halves are not treated as separable content. The theophany phrase 'the mountains quaked' recurs near-verbatim across the split (web:Isa.64.1's mountain-quaking wish and web:Isa.64.3's mountain-quaking report), a byte-true echo disclosed here rather than argued as a boundary.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A new first-person divine voice answers the unanswered question that closed the preceding unit, opening "נִדְרַ֨שְׁתִּי֙" (oshb:Isa.65.1, byte tier) (web:Isa.65.1, 'I am inquired of'), rendered “I am inquired of by those who didn't ask. I am found by those who didn't seek me.” (web:Isa.65.1) -- a speaker and scene change from the human communal voice of the preceding lament complex to Yahweh's own first-person self-disclosure, the tier-1 signal that opens this unit. The indictment of ongoing idolatrous practice (graves, secret places, forbidden meat, incense on the hills) continues through its own close, where the attribution "אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה" (oshb:Isa.65.7, byte tier) (web:Isa.65.7, 'says Yahweh'; this same verse also carries a ketiv/qere note, disclosed below) stands mid-verse, at tokens 5-6 of 19, before the relative clause naming the incense, and before the reproach and measuring clauses that follow it in the same verse; the disclosure inventory also records a SAMEKH paragraph break at oshb:Isa.65.7, tier-3 corroboration. A fresh koh-amar frame at oshb:Isa.65.8 (“Yahweh says”, web:Isa.65.8) opens a different, contrastive oracle and carries this unit's own close.

next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 65:1's 'not called by my name', לֹֽא קֹרָ֥א בִשְׁמִֽי (oshb:Isa.65.1, byte tier), as a direct continuation of the petition's 'not called by your name', לֹֽא נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ (oshb:Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.63.19, the split verse's first half, byte tier) -- the two clauses share only the negative particle לֹֽא at byte tier, meeting further only as a root-level tie on two roots, the call root and the name root -- was considered as a reason to merge the two units; it is rejected as a merge driver because 65:1 changes both the speaker (human petitioners to Yahweh himself) and the addressee (Yahweh to the nation), the stronger tier-1 signal, a ground the tier of the echo does not affect.

next_row.device_notes: Flagged as a genuine frontier question because 65:1's identity of 'a nation that was not called by my name' (rebellious Israel addressed ironically, per the surrounding indictment) against the covenant-naming denial of web:Isa.63.19 (the split verse's first half) raises an unresolved referent question the row does not decide. queue_items.claim: The cross-seam tie carries a byte-false position claim: the former-things noun does not open the next verse, and the row's own next clause names the token that does.
queue_items.grounds: oshb:Isa.65.17's first token is כִּֽי (byte tier); הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (byte tier) stands at token 10 of 14. At oshb:Isa.65.16 the same pointed form הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (byte tier) stands at token 15 of 18, whose final token is מֵעֵינָֽי (byte tier), so 'closing this unit' is a loose position claim as well. The byte-identity and the digit both re-verify: a sweep at that pointed form returns 2 verses book-wide at BYTE tier (MT 65:16, 65:17), against 3 verses accent-stripped and 5 skeleton -- the row's 'pointed form' qualifier is doing real work and is correctly stated.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair: replace 'closing this unit' / 'opening the next verse' with position-neutral wording (the same pointed form standing in both verses), or state the true token positions.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A second, formally distinct koh-amar frame opens the unit, "לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה" (oshb:Isa.65.13, byte tier) (web:Isa.65.13, 'therefore, thus says the Lord Yahweh'), a different divine-title form (adonai Yahweh) from the 65:8 frame's bare Yahweh. The oracle runs a fourfold contrast formula opened each time by הִנֵּ֨ה עֲבָדַ֤י (oshb:Isa.65.13, byte tier) -- three further instances, הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י and הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י (oshb:Isa.65.13) and הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י (oshb:Isa.65.14), byte-identical to each other and skeleton-identical to the first (sweep: 4 occurrences over 2 verses) -- “Behold, my servants will eat, but you will be hungry; behold, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty. Behold, my servants will rejoice, but you will be disappointed.” (web:Isa.65.13) plus a fourth pairing at 65:14 -- and closes at “because the former troubles are forgotten, and because they are hidden from my eyes.” (web:Isa.65.16), immediately before the unit ends and a new declaration, “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth” (web:Isa.65.17), opens a different oracle on a different subject (cosmic renewal rather than the servants/apostates contrast).

shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit to include the rest of the chapter's new-creation material as a single servants-and-new-creation oracle was considered, since both share the theme of reversal for the faithful; it is rejected because 65:17's 'For, behold, I create' introduces a new subject (cosmic renewal) and drops the servants/apostates contrast formula, with no tier-1 signal continuing the second-person 'you will be hungry' address beyond this row. This rejection stands despite two cross-seam ties not surfaced by the English rendering: the former-things noun closing this unit, הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.65.16, byte tier), is byte-identical to the same noun opening the next verse, הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier) -- sweep: 2 verses book-wide at that pointed form -- and the next verse itself opens on the subordinating connector כִּֽי (oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier); the election token crosses the same seam at skeleton tier (oshb:Isa.65.15 to oshb:Isa.65.22).

shipped_row.device_notes: Filed as judgment_oracle because the frame is triggered by 'therefore' (a consequence-clause marker) and its dominant declarative content is retribution on 'you' the addressees, even though 'my servants' blessing is embedded throughout as a contrastive counter-voice -- disclosed here as a one-sentence deviation. The fourfold 'behold, my servants ... but you' contrast formula recurs across 65:13-14 (sweep: 2 verses). The disclosure inventory records a petuchah break immediately before this unit (Isa.65.12) -- tier-3, single-witness, not a boundary driver.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar frame opens the unit, "כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה" (oshb:Isa.65.8, byte tier) (web:Isa.65.8, 'thus says Yahweh'), rendered “As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one says, 'Don't destroy it, for a blessing is in it:' so I will do for my servants' sake” (web:Isa.65.8), declaring the preservation of a remnant. The addressee pivots at “But you who forsake Yahweh” (web:Isa.65.11) into a judgment clause against apostates, still inside the same speech-frame opened at 65:8, closing at “but you did that which was evil in my eyes, and chose that in which I didn't delight.” (web:Isa.65.12). The unit ends there because 65:13 opens a new, formally marked koh-amar frame of its own ('therefore, thus says the Lord Yahweh'); the disclosure inventory records a petuchah break at this unit's own close (Isa.65.12).

Both the servant token and the election token continue past this unit's own close into the following oracle at skeleton tier (servant: sweep 7 tokens over 5 verses in this chapter; election: sweep 3 verses in this chapter). The disclosure inventory records a SAMEKH break immediately before this unit (Isa.65.7) and a petuchah break at its own close (Isa.65.12) -- tier-3, single-witness, not boundary drivers.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a fresh programmatic declaration introduced by the subordinating connector כִּֽי (oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier), "כִּֽי הִנְנִ֥י בוֹרֵ֛א שָׁמַ֥יִם חֲדָשִׁ֖ים וָאָ֣רֶץ חֲדָשָׁ֑ה" (oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier) (web:Isa.65.17, 'For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth'), rendered “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things will not be remembered, nor come into mind.” (web:Isa.65.17) -- a subject and register shift away from the retribution contrast of the preceding unit into cosmic renewal and Jerusalem's joy, even though the verse's own former-things noun, הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier), is byte-identical to the noun closing the immediately preceding verse, הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.65.16, byte tier) (sweep: 2 verses book-wide at that pointed form) -- an unmarked front-seam continuity the subject-and-register shift is argued against rather than around. It runs through the peaceable-kingdom vision, closing at “They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain,” says Yahweh.” (web:Isa.65.25), matching "אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Isa.65.25, byte tier) -- the postpositive speech signature, verse-final; the disclosure inventory records a SAMEKH break at this same closing verse, and the unit ends there because oshb:Isa.66.1 opens a new koh-amar frame, "כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה" (oshb:Isa.66.1, byte tier) (oshb:Isa.66.1, 'Yahweh says'), on a different subject (the temple and true worship).

queue_items.claim: The rejected alternative's ground -- that 66:1-2 and 66:3-4 remain inside one frame 'with no intervening tier-1 seam' -- is not byte-true as stated: an undisclosed divine-speech signature stands inside the span, at the caesura of the row's second verse.
queue_items.grounds: oshb:Isa.66.2 carries נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier) at tokens 9-10 of 20, standing on the verse's atnach; the same formula's book-wide census is 23 verses (verse count, skeleton tier), and the corpus treats it as a closure signal elsewhere in this same chapter. The shipped span nonetheless survives: the signature is mid-verse and oshb:Isa.66.2 continues past it with וְאֶל זֶ֣ה אַבִּ֔יט (byte tier) inside the same declaration, so it closes no verse. But neither boundary_rationale nor device_notes discloses it, while oshb:Isa.66.2 is already cited in boundary_evidence_refs for other content. All other checks on this row pass: the koh-amar onset, the catchword pair and the 7-verse trembling-root sweep (skeleton tier) re-verify exactly, and both bracketing SAMEKH marks match the inventory at MT 65:25 and MT 66:4 under the claimed type.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair: disclose the mid-verse divine-speech signature at oshb:Isa.66.2 and restate the rejection ground as positioned (no seam-eligible verse-final signal) rather than absolute.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A verse-initial koh-amar frame opens the book's final chapter, "כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה" (oshb:Isa.66.1, byte tier) (web:Isa.66.1, 'thus says Yahweh'), rendered “Yahweh says: "Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build to me?” (web:Isa.66.1).
